label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §3.4…: Blackburn proposes to explain the conceptual…
locator: §3.4, 'Since this sort of explanation makes reference to our purposes in using moral terms rather than to an independent realm of moral fact, Blackburn thinks it supports a quasi-realist account rather than a straightforward realist theory.'
interpretation: Blackburn (1993, 137, 143): moral judgments must supervene on natural ones because their point is 'to guide desires and choices among the natural features of the world'; since the explanation relies on what beliefs can coexist with linguistic competence, there is 'no further inference to a metaphysical conclusion'. Read as an explanation of why respecting supervenience is a requirement of competence, not as an answer to what makes a moral judgment true (Codex P1 on #189). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text). The typed Lean reading formalizes only the positive purposes-to-competence explanation, not a prohibition of other explanations, a full semantics of supervenience or a metaphysical conclusion.
